change.nodeGuard: Use source instanceof IncomingMessage from node:http, which matches the actual default NodeHttpServer request source and its subclasses.
change.singleConsumer: The Node branch never calls HttpServerRequest.toWeb, so it does not create the old Effect body stream in addition to the native stream.
change.body: Use node:stream Readable.toWeb only for methods other than GET/HEAD. Preserve raw bytes and streaming; no full buffering, body parsing, retries or synthetic response.
change.metadata: Use the same pinned HttpServerRequest.toURL and sanitized headers/method as the existing Effect conversion; retain the existing host, proxy-header sanitization, exact origin and Microsoft public-origin adapter checks.
change.fallback: Non-Node sources retain the existing HttpServerRequest.toWeb fallback, including an existing native Web Request source.
change.signal: The existing Effect.tryPromise callback and installation.handler(new Request(request, {signal})) remain byte-for-byte unchanged. No weaker grant or fake signal is introduced.
change.lifecycle: Return composition, privacy layer, mount, transport, original installation.dispose and response handling are unchanged. Native toWeb owns pause/resume/finished/cancel handling for this one request stream.
change.limits: No limit constants or body readers change. Local canonical JSON readCommand retains its 2MiB configured maximum; product routes retain their existing bounded parsers. The global BodyLimit still rejects declared oversized Content-Length. Neither this candidate nor the existing Effect stream path proves enforcement of MaxBodySize for an arbitrary chunked stream.
change.error: An invalid toURL result throws within the existing route effect and retains the catchCause→503 behavior; origin mismatches remain 403.
